headline: Salah becomes Egypt's all-time top scorer with a Panenka penalty
facts: Salah scored twice in Egypt's 5-0 AFCON qualifier win over Malawi.
His second goal, a Panenka penalty in added time, was his 70th for Egypt and gave him the outright national record, after he first tied Hossam Hassan with his 84th-minute goal.
Salah is 34, now plays for Trabzonspor and has nine goals in 11 Turkish Super Lig games this season.
background: Salah left Liverpool for Trabzonspor at the start of 2026-27; at Liverpool he became the club's all-time Premier League top scorer with 191 goals.

headline: AFCON 2027 qualifying window: nine teams through, Nigeria on the brink
facts: Nine teams have qualified: Morocco, Mali, Senegal, Cameroon, Benin and Burkina Faso joined co-hosts Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.
Senegal threw away a two-goal lead against Sudan but drew 2-2 and still qualified; Nigeria lost 3-0 to Guinea-Bissau and drew 0-0 in Tanzania.
Algeria lost 3-0 to Togo and Tunisia are bottom of their group; the last 15 places will be decided in March 2027.
background: AFCON 2027 is hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from 19 June to 17 July 2027, the first AFCON in East Africa since 1976.

headline: Nigeria could miss AFCON 2027 as striker woes continue
facts: Nigeria drew 0-0 away to Tanzania in Zanzibar and have 7 points from 4 games in Group L.
Only one qualifying place is open because Tanzania qualified as co-hosts; Guinea-Bissau lead the group after beating Nigeria 3-0.
Nigeria must win both March games, the second by at least four goals, and have scored nothing in either away game this campaign.
background: Nigeria missed the 2026 World Cup and have a long record as a three-time AFCON winner, so missing the 2027 finals would be a major shock.
footage_terms: Nigeria Super Eagles Chelle press conference

headline: CAS to rule on Senegal v Morocco AFCON final dispute by end of November
facts: In January Senegal beat host Morocco in the final after their players walked off in protest at a late Morocco penalty; Morocco's penalty was then saved and Senegal scored the only goal in extra time.
In March CAF overturned the result and awarded Morocco a 3-0 default win; Senegal appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport.
CAS held its hearing on 8 October in Lausanne and said a ruling is expected by the end of November.
background: The final in Rabat saw a 15-minute stoppage and fan clashes; Morocco currently hold the title only through the CAF ruling.
footage_terms: Senegal Morocco AFCON final walk off
Senegal Morocco final penalty saved Brahim Diaz

headline: CAF reverses four-year AFCON plan and restores two-year cycle
facts: CAF's executive committee unanimously reversed its December 2025 decision to play AFCON every four years after 2028.
CAF said the planned Africa Nations League would take years to generate the needed revenue.
Next tournaments are 2027, 2028, 2031 and 2033, leaving a three-year gap after 2028.
background: CAF announced the four-year plan in December 2025 alongside a proposed $1 billion commercial tender; many players and coaches opposed it.

headline: Lookman hurt: Atletico star out of Nigeria game with knee ligament sprain
facts: A scan confirmed a knee ligament sprain, ruling Lookman out of Nigeria's qualifier in Zanzibar.
He was hurt in the 3-1 win over Tanzania in Uyo after setting up Alhassan Yusuf's opener.
Atletico face four games in 11 days from 22 November; Lookman's availability is unclear.
background: Lookman is a Nigeria international who now plays for Atletico Madrid; Nigeria were also without Victor Osimhen in this window.

headline: Mofokeng scores late brace as South Africa beat Kenya in Nairobi
facts: South Africa won 2-1 away to Kenya in an AFCON qualifier, with Mofokeng scoring both goals late on.
Mofokeng left Orlando Pirates in the off-season for Union Saint-Gilloise in Belgium.
The article says Bafana's defence was weak on set pieces and aerial balls despite the win.
background: Pitso Mosimane returned as Bafana coach; an earlier 2-2 home draw with Kenya drew criticism over his team selection.

headline: Ajax striker Arokodare in huge form, but Nigeria still stuck
facts: Arokodare has 13 goals and 4 assists in 17 games for Ajax this season, including 7 in the Eredivisie and 6 in the Conference League.
He scored twice against Tanzania in Nigeria's 3-1 win, taking him to 4 goals in 13 caps.
Osimhen and Lookman were unavailable, making Arokodare Nigeria's lead striker candidate.
background: Arokodare moved to Ajax after a difficult spell at Wolves and has said he wanted to move past it.

headline: Bayern and Ajax to open new Nairobi stadium on 5 January
facts: Bayern and Ajax will play a friendly in Nairobi on 5 January to open the new Raila Odinga International Stadium.
The clubs last met in December 2018, a 3-3 Champions League draw with four goals in the last 10 minutes.
Bayern's only previous games in Africa were at the 2013 Club World Cup in Morocco, which they won.
background: The stadium is a venue for AFCON 2027, the first AFCON in East Africa since 1976.
footage_terms: Bayern Munich Club World Cup 2013 final Raja

headline: Nigeria draw 3-3 with Russia as brothers debut together
facts: Nigeria drew 3-3 with Russia in Nizhny Novgorod; Iheanacho scored about 10 minutes in, his 15th goal for Nigeria.
Russia led 3-1 before 19-year-old debutant Peter Edokpolor and a stoppage-time Akor Adams goal rescued the draw.
Abubakar and Abdullahi Umar became the first brothers to debut for Nigeria in the same match.
background: Coach Eric Chelle named five debutants in a heavily rotated side.

headline: Samson Adamu confirmed as first Nigerian CAF general secretary
facts: Adamu is the first Nigerian to hold the CAF general secretary job permanently since CAF was founded in 1957.
He had been acting in the role since 29 March after Veron Mosengo-Omba.
His father Amos Adamu, a former FIFA executive, was banned by FIFA for three years in 2010 over ethics violations, upheld by CAS in 2012.
background: Adamu joined CAF in 2018 as director of competitions and had earlier spent about a decade at Kinetic Sport Management.

headline: Hakimi hat-trick and two assists as PSG beat Le Havre 5-1
facts: Hakimi scored his first career hat-trick and added two assists as PSG came from behind to win 5-1 at Le Havre on 30 October.
He became the only defender to register five goal contributions in a Ligue 1 game, having never had more than two in 135 league games before.
ESPN calls him favourite for the 2026 CAF African Footballer of the Year, awarded in Lagos on 7 December.
background: Hakimi joined PSG from Inter Milan in 2021 and won the 2025 CAF award, the first defender to do so since 1973 per ESPN.

headline: Egypt sack coach Hossam Hassan after Salah friction, appoint Ali Maher
facts: Egypt dismissed coach Hossam Hassan on 7 November, about four months after losing to Argentina at the World Cup.
Local press had scrutinised his relationship with Salah, who was substituted against Angola and later left camp before the South Sudan trip.
Former international Ali Maher replaced him; Egypt then drew 0-0 with Malawi in his second game.
background: Hassan is a former Egypt striker whose all-time scoring record of 69 national-team goals Salah has now passed.
footage_terms: Ali Maher Egypt coach press conference

headline: Kenya coach Benni McCarthy in row over unpaid allowances and booing fans
facts: Kenya drew 2-2 at Orlando Stadium, then lost 2-1 at home to South Africa in the double-header.
McCarthy alleged players refused to train over unpaid allowances and demanded payment for himself, his staff and the squad.
His remarks about booing fans and his own comfortable lifestyle drew criticism and he later apologised.
background: McCarthy is a former South Africa striker who won a domestic title as Orlando Pirates coach; Kenya are already qualified for AFCON 2027 as co-hosts.

headline: Tunisia players walk off in Libya over disputed penalty
facts: Tunisia protested a disputed penalty in Tripoli and several players walked off the pitch; Libya's Ezoo El Maremi scored from the spot.
Captain Ferjani Sassi reportedly objected to fans being present.
Tunisia are preparing a complaint to CAF and sit bottom of Group H with three points from four games.
background: Tunisia are a regular AFCON qualifier and played at the 2026 World Cup, so bottom of the group is a sharp fall.

headline: Ghana's interim coach ends eight-game winless run after Queiroz exit
facts: Carlos Queiroz left Ghana by mutual consent on about 1 October, his second exit in under three months, after a 2-0 loss in Ivory Coast and a 4-2 home loss to Gambia from 2-0 up.
Interim coach Kim Bjorkegren won both games against Somalia in November, ending an eight-match winless run in AFCON qualifying.
Ghana still need to appoint a permanent coach.
background: Ghana reached the 2026 World Cup round of 32 before losing 1-0 to Colombia, then Queiroz returned as coach after that exit.

headline: Iwobi leads the Premier League in expected assists for Fulham
facts: Iwobi leads the Premier League in expected assists with 2.95 this season.
He is tied with Bruno Fernandes for most passes completed into the penalty area.
He has set up two or more shots in each of Fulham's last seven league games.
background: Iwobi, 30, broke through at Arsenal and plays for Nigeria, whose attack was short of creativity in this qualifying window.

headline: Osimhen linked with Manchester United while recovering from knee surgery
facts: Goal, citing The Sun, reports Osimhen is open to joining United and willing to match his Galatasaray salary; this is unconfirmed.
He is under contract at Galatasaray until June 2029 with no release clause, valued by Turkish sources at 80-100 million pounds.
ESPN reported separately that he is out for Nigeria after knee surgery.
background: Osimhen joined Galatasaray on loan from Napoli in 2024 and later signed permanently; he scored 37 goals in all competitions in his first season there.

headline: Fulham boss says Bassey is among the world's best defenders amid United link
facts: Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa said Bassey is one of the best central defenders in the world and Fulham should not sell him this winter.
British outlets linked Bassey with Manchester United earlier in the week.
Fulham are 15th, two points above 18th-placed United; Bassey's contract runs to mid-2027 with a one-year option.
background: Bassey, a Nigeria defender, moved from Rangers to Ajax for 23 million euros in 2022 and joined Fulham a year later for 22 million.

headline: Son and Bouanga carry LAFC into MLS playoff series against St. Louis
facts: LAFC, the No. 6 seed, face No. 3 St. Louis City in MLS playoff Round 1 starting Monday.
Son has 7 goals and 6 assists since the World Cup after going without a goal before the tournament.
ESPN says LAFC underperformed for much of 2026; two of four writers pick LAFC, citing Son as due a big game.
background: Son left Tottenham for LAFC in 2025 after a long Spurs career; Bouanga leads LAFC with 18 goals and 9 assists this season.

headline: Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia postponed to December 2027 over security concerns
facts: The AFC postponed the tournament, originally 7 January to 5 February 2027, citing regional security concerns.
The new dates are 23 December 2027 to 21 January 2028, still needing FIFA approval.
The AFC president had said last month that preparations were continuing as planned.
background: Saudi Arabia is hosting the Asian Cup for the first time and will also host the 2034 World Cup; Riyadh was due to host 30 of 51 matches.
footage_terms: Asian Cup Saudi Arabia stadium Riyadh

headline: Moriyasu's Japan era ends with a 2-1 loss to Paraguay
facts: Moriyasu's 113-match spell as Japan coach ended with a 2-1 friendly loss to Paraguay in Singapore.
Paraguay led 2-0 from two set pieces; Shio Fukuda scored on debut in the 85th minute.
He leaves with a 68 percent win rate, wins over Brazil, England, Spain, Germany and Uruguay, and no knockout-round win in two World Cups.
background: Moriyasu took Japan from 55th to 17th in the world rankings; he has been linked to Malaysia but no offer has been made, per ESPN.

headline: Kubo scores as Japan beat Brazil 3-2 in Singapore
facts: Japan won 3-2 in the Mizuho Blue Challenge at Singapore's National Stadium before 38,688 fans.
Kubo scored after 15 minutes, Keito Nakamura after 19 and Tatsuhiro Sakamoto in injury time; Vinicius Junior scored both Brazil goals.
It was revenge for the World Cup, where Brazil beat Japan with a 95th-minute goal.
background: This was Hajime Moriyasu's penultimate match as Japan coach; he left after the loss to Paraguay three days later.

headline: South Korea's Asian Games stars apologise for military exemption remarks
facts: South Korea beat Japan 1-0 in the Asian Games final through a goal by Swansea's Eom Jisung, a fourth straight title.
Tottenham's Yang Min-hyeok, on loan at Westerlo, said the military exemption was the real prize; he and teammates later apologised.
Gold in the Asian Games exempts able-bodied Korean men from military service.
background: South Korean men must normally serve in the military before turning 28, which makes Asian Games gold a major career prize.
footage_terms: South Korea Japan Asian Games final highlights
Asian Games football final Korea gold

headline: Japan's Tashima says Balogun red-card saga pushed him to run against Infantino
facts: Kozo Tashima says FIFA suspending Folarin Balogun's automatic World Cup ban, after Donald Trump said he asked Infantino to review it, led him to run for FIFA president.
The vote in March 2027 is Infantino's first contested election since 2016; France's Philippe Diallo, backed by UEFA, is the other challenger.
Infantino has the support of the Asian and African confederations; Tashima says he may fund his campaign by crowdfunding.
background: Tashima, 68, is honorary president of the Japan FA and has sat on the FIFA Council since 2015.

headline: Algeria repays Kansas for World Cup base camp welcome
facts: 38 residents of Lawrence, Kansas visited Algeria from 9 to 15 November, paid for by the Algerian government as thanks for hosting the team at the World Cup.
Algeria used Lawrence as its official base camp, with the University of Kansas band playing its anthem before training.
President Tebboune ordered a twinning agreement between Tipaza and Kansas City.
background: Algeria was one of 50 countries whose visa applicants faced a 10,000 dollar bond requirement, so few Algerian fans could travel to the tournament.
footage_terms: Algeria Lawrence Kansas World Cup base camp

headline: Nicolas Jackson's Aston Villa form leaves Chelsea fans asking questions
facts: Chelsea let Jackson leave in August for an initial 47.5 million pounds.
He scored twice in Villa's 2-1 win over Manchester City that ended City's perfect league start.
He has seven goals in all competitions, including a double in a 6-0 Champions League win over Fenerbahce.
background: Unai Emery gave Jackson his La Liga debut at Villarreal in 2021, and Jackson scored 12 league goals in 2022-23.

headline: Baleba hamstring blow adds to Man United injury woes
facts: Baleba hurt his hamstring in United's 3-2 Champions League win over Roma and went off early in the second half.
Michael Carrick said he will be out for a number of weeks.
The win ended a nine-game winless run and left United just above the relegation zone.
background: Baleba, 22 and a Cameroon international, joined United from Brighton for about 70 million pounds in the summer and had an ankle injury before his debut.

headline: Man City's 85 million pound teenager Bouaddi starts to deliver
facts: Bouaddi, 19, joined City for a reported 85 million pounds and is seen as a possible successor to Rodri.
In his first league start he made 93 touches, third-highest in the match, with seven line-breaking passes.
Enzo Maresca said he is very good and that City should avoid putting pressure on him.
background: Maresca now manages City after Pep Guardiola; Bouaddi is a Morocco international.

headline: Brighton teenager Zadok Yohanna leads Nigeria's Olympic qualifying squad
facts: Yohanna, 19, leads Nigeria's 23-man U23 squad for the African qualifiers against DR Congo, with legs on 13 and 17 November.
He joined Brighton from AIK this offseason on a five-year deal after five goals and four assists in 18 games for the Swedish club.
Nigeria last reached the Olympics in 2016, winning bronze in Rio.
background: Winning the tie sends Nigeria to the final qualifying round in March for the 2027 U23 AFCON in Egypt, a route to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

headline: Hull's Belloumi silences pundits with equaliser against Everton
facts: After pundits joked that Belloumi was dropped because he was tired, he came on in the 65th minute and equalised in the 74th at 2-2 against Everton.
He has three goals and two assists in six Premier League games, leading Hull's scoring.
He scored twice in an earlier 2-2 draw with Chelsea.
background: Belloumi, 24, is the son of Algerian legend Lakhdar Belloumi and made his Algeria debut in a 3-1 AFCON qualifier win over Zambia.
footage_terms: Hull City Premier League highlights Belloumi

headline: Ivory Coast's Yalcouye scores on debut under returning coach Renard
facts: Renard started his second Ivory Coast spell with two wins and two clean sheets, beating Ghana 2-0 in Bouake.
Brighton midfielder Malick Yalcouye scored on debut in that win, with Yann Gboho also scoring.
In November, Yalcouye scored the opener in a 2-1 win over Gambia, and Ivory Coast lead Group C by three points.
background: Renard led Ivory Coast to the AFCON title eleven years earlier; Yalcouye is a 21-year-old midfielder.
footage_terms: Herve Renard Ivory Coast press conference

headline: Spain's football chief claims 2030 World Cup final can only be in Spain, Morocco objects
facts: Spanish FA president Rafael Louzan said the 2030 final can and will only be held in Spain, arguing Portugal lacks an 80,000-seat stadium.
Morocco wants the final at the planned 115,000-seat King Hassan II Stadium, and FIFA has not decided.
FIFA earlier denied a report that Infantino offered Morocco the final while seeking support for his re-election.
background: Spain's 2024 bid listed three possible final venues: the Bernabeu, Camp Nou and one stadium in Morocco.
footage_terms: World Cup 2030 Morocco stadium Hassan II
